sources.cite: Microsoft Learn (Azure Monitor), Set daily cap on Log Analytics workspace
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-18. When the cap is reached, collection of billable data stops 'for the rest of a 24-hour period'; 'When the daily cap is met, you are effectively blind to the current state of your monitored environment'; 'Data collection resumes at the reset time which is a different hour of the day for each workspace. This reset hour can't be configured'; the cap 'should not be used as a primary mechanism to filter or reduce data before ingestion... Instead, use ingestion-time transformations'; create an alert before the cap is hit; sample query: _LogOperation | where Category =~ 'Ingestion' | where Detail contains 'OverQuota'. That a workspace-based Application Insights resource stops showing new telemetry when its workspace cap is reached is the author's reading of the same page.

brief.situation: You are the DevOps engineer at Halden Ticketing. Checkout errors started around 11:00, but Application Insights shows no telemetry at all since 11:20: no requests, no exceptions, no traces. The workspace-based resource writes to workspace law-tickets, which has a 20 GB daily cap. This morning's 10:05 release changed the log level. The 13:00 on-sale for a stadium tour needs checkout working, and the team cannot debug blind.
handover: The workspace's cap resets at 02:00 (fixed per workspace).
The release pipeline sets Logging__LogLevel__Default from a variable group.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the checkout service's telemetry, the workspace's daily cap and the dashboards the team reads.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

source.note: The on-sale starts at 13:00, 50 minutes after the page; the team needs telemetry to find the checkout errors before then.

writeup.question: For the record: why telemetry stopped, what you changed, and what stops a repeat.

parts.label: Why
parts.modelAnswer: The 10:05 release set Debug from a variable group shared with staging; traces rose 40-fold and the workspace hit its 20 GB cap at 11:20, which stops collection until the 02:00 reset.

parts.label: Changed
parts.modelAnswer: Set the log level to Information and raised today's cap to 30 GB; collection resumed and the payment timeouts showed. Deleting the workspace destroys history; a restart changes nothing.

parts.label: Repeat
parts.modelAnswer: Per-environment variable groups, an alert at 80% of the cap, and an ingestion-time transformation that drops Debug traces.

expertPath.text: OverQuota at 11:20; AppTraces 18.7 GB; log level Debug; reset 02:00.
Information; cap 30 GB today; split groups, 80% alert, transformation.

historyLost.headline: Raise the cap; never delete the workspace
historyLost.body: The daily cap is a setting. Lower the volume that caused it and raise the cap for today; deleting the workspace destroys history and breaks every connection to it.

onsaleBlind.headline: A reached cap means no telemetry until the reset
onsaleBlind.body: When the daily cap is met collection stops for the rest of the 24-hour period; find the volume that caused it and act now.

telemetryBack.headline: Good: restore visibility, then remove the cause
telemetryBack.body: You confirmed the cap, found the 40-fold trace volume from Debug logging, set Information and raised today's cap, checked telemetry flowed, and separated environments with an 80% alert and an ingestion filter.

scoring.modelReasoning: No telemetry at all since one minute is a collection problem, not an app one: the workspace logged OverQuota at 11:20. Today's traces are 40 times yesterday's because the release set Debug. Set Information, raise today's cap so collection resumes, and check exceptions arrive. Deleting the workspace loses history; a restart leaves both causes. Then split the settings by environment, alert before the cap, and drop Debug traces at ingestion.
